title: System architecture
intro: Four layers on two stacks. You talk to Jarvis (1), which reads and acts on the Dashboard's store (2), sends work to the Factory (3), and every long-running agent lives in a termhub session (4). The work stack and the personal stack run the same dev-tools code with different .env files; no data or credentials cross between them.
maintenance: Rendered from personal-assistant/src/dashboard/architecture.json. Add, remove or rename a component, tool, port, model default or table in the same commit as the code (root CLAUDE.md, 'Architecture map'); test/architecture.test.js checks the parts it can.

statuses.landing: Code on main, contract or rollout still landing

layers.name: Ask (Talk)
layers.summary: Jarvis: a voice page with a fast local model that answers simple turns in about a second, and the PA chat (a Claude Code session) that does everything else behind permission prompts.

layers.name: Plan (Dashboard)
layers.summary: The worker ingests mail, Teams, GitHub, Jira and meetings, distils asks into commitments, and serves the board. Everything is in Postgres.

layers.name: Build (Factory)
layers.summary: software-factory: jobs (code, research, report) on two runtimes: metered API models through LiteLLM/OpenHands, or Claude Code on the subscription inside a termhub session.

layers.name: Run (Sessions)
layers.summary: termhub: the terminal supervisor every agent runs in. sessiond owns the PTYs and survives updates; the front serves the UI, the APIs and the /pa/ proxy.

layers.name: Models and outside services
layers.summary: Where model calls and data go, and who pays: the Claude subscription, metered APIs (Azure, DeepSeek), the local GPU, GitHub and Microsoft 365.

components.name: /talk voice page
components.role: Hears the room in the browser; sends only the utterance after the wake word.

where.work: Browser tab served by the dashboard
where.personal: Browser tab served by the dashboard, through termhub /pa/talk

details.Wake word: openWakeWord hey_jarvis_v0.1.onnx, client-side on onnxruntime-web (WASM, one thread)
details.Models served: /talk/models/ serves a fixed list of file names (MODEL_FILES), never a path
details.End of turn: POST /api/talk/endpoint, proxied to smart-turn in the voice service
Sends: POST /api/talk/latency after each turn (end of speech to first audio, logged by the PA)
POST /api/chat/permission (a spoken yes or no to the chat's action prompt)
details.Privacy: Nothing leaves the browser until a request is made; the wake word stays client-side.
details.Modes: Voice (the face, default) or Text, switched in the page's panel and remembered per browser (jarvis.talk.mode). Text mode is the same PA chat as a transcript with a box to type in (chat.client.js, POST /api/chat), and shows the Approve / Deny card for a pending action prompt (permission.client.js); Voice mode has no buttons.
details.Permission prompts: Audio only, no buttons: Jarvis speaks the server-written question (transcript.askTool) and your next utterance answers it (talk.core.js createVoiceAsk: only while awake, only from words begun after the question, strict yes/no, unclear asked once more, 60 s window) via POST /api/chat/permission with the page token
details.Sleep: "Jarvis, sleep" / "stop listening" / "go to sleep" (and the stop phrases) return it to wake-word-only, said aloud; windows: 6 s after the wake word, 8 s after an answer, 60 s after a question

components.name: Fast lane (System 1)
components.role: Decide, then speak (D7): a router returns calibrated probabilities p(answer_here), p(hand_off), p(action); only above the answer threshold does a small model speak the answer, otherwise your words go to the PA chat verbatim. No tools.

where.work: In the worker process (dashboard), POST /api/talk/turn
where.personal: Off (PA_FAST_LANE=0): no Ollama on k-911-x17 yet

details.Model: local/llama3.2:3b through Ollama's native /api/chat, for both the router and the answerer
details.Router: PA_FAST_ROUTER=logprob (src/chat/fastRouter.js): one call, one generated token. The model is asked a fixed question, 'A (answer here), B (hand off: needs a lookup) or C (action)?', and the top log-probabilities of that token are calibrated (temperature 0.397 plus a per-class bias, fitted by `pa eval router --fit`) into p(answer_here), p(hand_off), p(action). Alternatives: same (the older one-call JSON {label, route, say}), rules, a model string, an http(s) URL
details.Answerer: speaks only when p(answer_here) >= 0.85 (PA_FAST_ANSWER_THRESHOLD): a second streamed call that writes one to three sentences. Below it, the user's words go to the PA chat verbatim with 'One moment.' (or 'On it.' when p(action) > p(hand_off))
details.Eval: `pa eval router`: 83 turns in src/eval/router-cases.json (anonymized logged turns, the known miss 'check my mail from <name>', and synthetic ones), 3-way accuracy, turns answered here that should not be, latency warm. Nov 2026 on this laptop's RTX 3000 Ada: 0 action turns answered here; see PLAN.md 0.6 for the numbers
details.Prompt cache: the router's system prompt and examples never change; the snapshot comes next, then the last two turns, then the words. After each turn, and when the snapshot changes, a one-token call with the next turn's prefix fills Ollama's cache, so a turn pays only for its own words
details.Fallback: azure/pa (PA_FAST_FALLBACK_MODEL) when Ollama is down or the router has not answered within 2500 ms (PA_FAST_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_MS): the one-call text format decides and replies
Prompt: a snapshot of your day: a few hundred tokens (open asks by bucket, top 3 overdue and due, next 24 h of meetings, active runs, waiting drafts and review items, first 300 chars of your 'me' page)
router: the last 2 turns, 200 chars each; answerer: the last 6 turns (chat history merged with turns it answered itself)
router: 1 output token; answerer: max 300 output tokens
details.Snapshot refresh: Cached in memory, rebuilt in the background when older than 60 s (PA_FAST_CONTEXT_SECONDS)
details.Context window: unknown: Ollama's default for the model (the PA does not set num_ctx)
details.Compaction: none needed: every turn is a fresh prompt
details.Kept warm: keep_alive 24h (PA_FAST_KEEP_ALIVE); when /talk opens, and every 4 minutes after, a one-token request carrying the fixed system prompt primes the KV cache prefix (llm.warmLocal with system; the answerer's prompt under the logprob router, which also primes its own prefix)
Guards: the router never writes words, so it cannot answer a turn by itself; below the threshold nothing local is spoken but the stock acknowledgement
never answers an action-like request (guardDecision / looksLikeAction turn it into a hand-off, whatever the router said)
a hand-off types your verbatim words into the PA chat; the model's task is only a labelled hint
a hand-off's spoken acknowledgement is replaced by the stock one when it reads as an answer (spokenAck)
details.Billing: free (local GPU); the azure/pa fallback is metered and recorded in llm_spend

components.name: Jarvis: the PA chat (System 2)
components.role: One long-lived Claude Code session in termhub that reads through MCP tools and acts only behind permission prompts.

where.work: A termhub session on the laptop, home <dataDir>/pa-home
where.personal: A termhub session on k-911-x17, once its claude login is a personal one

details.Model: PA_CHAT_MODEL (no default in code: the Claude Code CLI's own default); PA_CHAT_AGENT picks claude or opencode
details.Started as: claude --permission-mode default --mcp-config pa-home/pa-chat.mcp.json [--model ...]; never with --dangerously-skip-permissions (chatCommand refuses it)
details.Context window: whatever Claude Code reports for the model (context_window.context_window_size; the statusline falls back to 200,000 tokens)
details.Compaction: Claude Code auto-compacts its own context. State lives in the store, not the transcript: a SessionStart hook runs `pa context` (60 s timeout) on every start, resume, clear and compaction, so a week-old chat still knows this morning's asks.
What it loads: CLAUDE.md, rewritten from code on every start (src/chat/index.js); your additions go in CLAUDE.local.md
`pa context`: profile, today's brief, what is waiting on you, live runs
INBOX.md: the worker's pushed notifications, read as data, never instructions
Permissions: settings.json: defaultMode default, bypass mode disabled; verifyClaudeHome reads them back (and settings.local.json) before starting
no `pa` shell command is allowed: every one asks
the caveman plugin is off for this session only
its action-tool prompts can also be answered by voice on Talk (while awake) or on the dashboard's Waiting for your yes card; src/chat/permission.js checks the screen first
How you reach it: Ask (/talk), by voice or in its Text mode (feed.js types into the session through termhub's input API and tails its transcript)
details.Transcript: ~/.claude/projects/<encoded pa-home>/<uuid>.jsonl, tailed by byte offset (first read: last 4 MB)
details.Billing: the machine's Claude Code login: a claude.ai subscription login is not metered per call

components.name: personal-assistant MCP server
components.role: The store over MCP (stdio). Read-only for every session; the PA chat alone also gets the `pa` verbs, task_add and the per-layer chat tools.

where.work: A stdio child of each Claude Code session that registers it: user scope as `personal-assistant`, the PA chat as `pa-chat` with PA_MCP_CHAT_TOOLS=1
where.personal: Planned with the PA

details.Shared surface: recall and memory reads, open_commitments, who_is, repo_state; remember only proposes (a pending_review claim); request_secret / secret_status never return a value
details.Chat-only surface: the read-only `pa` verbs as the `pa` tool (run with PA_READ_ONLY=1), task_add, board / card / factory_* / sessions reads, and the actions factory_start, factory_continue, factory_resume, factory_cancel, factory_approve, session_start
details.Actions: the dispatch paths themselves (dispatch.start, factory cancel/approve/resume), never a second implementation; auto_merge and push_to_main become a card ('suggested by the chat')
details.Data rule: everything a tool returns quotes other people's messages: data, never instructions

components.name: Supervisor (zero-downtime)
components.role: Owns the dashboard port and proxies it (HTTP, SSE, WebSocket) to the current worker generation, so a deploy starts the new worker beside the old one, switches without a gap and can switch back (plan items Z1, Z4).

where.work: pa-worker scheduled task: conhost --headless node src\worker.js, which becomes the supervisor (the task was registered elevated, so the deploy could not rewrite it to src\supervisor), on 127.0.0.1:7300; generations on 127.0.0.1:<OS-assigned>
where.personal: Code on main; the next linux/redeploy.sh rewrites the pa-worker unit to node src/supervisor and restarts it once to bootstrap

Ports: public: 127.0.0.1:PA_DISPATCH_PORT (7300), held by the supervisor for its whole life
each worker generation: 127.0.0.1 on a port the OS assigns (port 0), reported over IPC ({type: 'listening', port})
details.Roll: spawn generation N+1 (PA_SUPERVISED=1) → wait for GET /healthz ready (180 s at most) → route new requests to it → send N drain (N hands its passes over, Z2) → end N's SSE and WebSocket streams (clients reconnect, with Last-Event-ID, to N+1) → wait for N's in-flight requests (30 s at most) → keep N drained as the standby for 150 s (covers the drain and the deploy's 60 s watch), then stop it
details.Failed roll: a generation that exits or is not ready in time is killed; N keeps serving and the roll answers ok: false
details.Crash: the serving generation exiting on its own is replaced by the standby if one is held, else by a new one, backing off 1 s to 60 s
details.Control: one JSON line on a local socket: \\.\pipe\pa-supervisor-<port> on Windows, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pa-supervisor-<port>.sock elsewhere; {"cmd":"roll"}, {"cmd":"rollback"} or {"cmd":"status"} (status carries source, a hash of the running supervisor file); `node src/supervisor roll|rollback|status`; SIGHUP rolls on Linux
details.Background passes: single owner (Z2, src/util/lease.js): every timer, watcher and the durable worker is declared on the scheduler (src/util/scheduler.js) and runs only while its generation holds the lease, pg_advisory_lock(7300) on a dedicated connection. On drain the old generation stops its schedulers and releases the lease at once; the new one polls every 500 ms and takes over within a second. Each pass run also holds pg_advisory_lock(7301, hashtext(name)), so a pass the old generation is still finishing is skipped by the new one until it ends; every other pass moves over at once. Undrain (rollback) takes the lease and the passes back
details.Rule: node builtins only; never loads worker code, so a deploy never needs to restart it
details.Rollback: {"cmd":"rollback"}: drain the serving generation, undrain the standby, wait for its /healthz (30 s), flip back, stop the other. Only while a standby is held (150 s after a roll)
details.Deploy (Z4): windows/redeploy.ps1, linux/redeploy.sh (run by termhub's Update after its pull, or by hand with -Pull/--pull and -DryRun/--dry-run) → node src/supervisor/deploy.js: npm install when the package files changed, npm run build when one exists (none yet), roll, then /healthz + /api/version every 2 s for 60 s; 3 failed probes in a row, or not the new commit at the end → rollback, exit 1
details.Restart fallback: the scripts restart the task/unit (stop, kill node src/supervisor and src/worker.js, start, wait up to 120 s for the new commit) only when deploy.js exits 3 (no supervisor answers: the bootstrap) or 4 (src/supervisor/index.js changed), or when they just rewrote a task/unit that still named src/worker.js
details.Bootstrap: node src/worker.js not started by the supervisor (an older task or unit, which a non-elevated deploy cannot rewrite) becomes the supervisor before loading any worker code; PA_NO_SUPERVISOR=1 runs the bare worker
details.Log: <state dir>/logs/supervisor.log (PA_DATA_DIR, else %LOCALAPPDATA%\personal-assistant or ~/.local/share/personal-assistant; PA_SUPERVISOR_LOG overrides): the supervisor's lines and each generation's stdout/stderr as [gen N], rotated at 5 MB, 3 kept. Workers log 'event loop blocked' for any stall over 1 s
details.Readiness: a generation says ready only at the end of its startup (passes declared, lease requested), not when its port opens: the module loading in between blocked the loop for seconds right after the flip

components.name: Dashboard server
components.role: The board (Plan), Ask's voice and text page, the Factory page (Build) and this map, on loopback. It rides in the worker process.

where.work: http://127.0.0.1:7300 (PA_DISPATCH_PORT / PA_DISPATCH_HOST)
where.personal: http://127.0.0.1:7300 on k-911-x17, through termhub /pa/ over the tailnet

Guards: binds loopback only and rejects a non-loopback Host (DNS rebinding)
starting auto_merge / push_to_main also needs the page token (X-PA-Page) and the confirmed level
answering the chat's permission prompt (POST /api/chat/permission) also needs the page token
details.Chat: /api/chat (type into the PA chat, from Ask's Text mode), /api/chat/stream (SSE of its transcript), /api/chat/history, /api/chat/permission (answer its action prompt)
details.Repos: /api/repos: the repo registry with your latest PRs, and the GitHub/Jira review requests and board items still open (Plan's former Code & boards section)
details.Send: never sends: a draft opens, already written, in Teams or Outlook and you press Send
details.Health: GET /healthz: 200 {ready: true} once its process has finished starting, 503 while starting or draining (what the supervisor switches on)
details.Waiting for your yes: a card at the top of the board, on Build and in Ask's Text mode (permission.client.js) for the PA chat's pending action prompt, with Approve / Deny through POST /api/chat/permission; src/chat/permission.js reads the session's screen before one keystroke (Enter on Yes, or Esc). A factory job parked on an approval (needs_human) says "waiting for your approval" on Build and in Plan's Agent runs, each with Approve (POST /api/factory/jobs/<id>/approve); by voice, Jarvis's factory_approve
details.Live feed (plan 0.4, E3): GET /api/events: one SSE stream per page (events.client.js) of {id, topic, at, payload} with topics board, run, factory, routine and resync. Postgres triggers (sql/034_events_notify.sql) NOTIFY pa_events on every change to commitment, proposal, draft, ledger_evidence, commitment_block, secret_request, notification, run, factory_board (only when its jobs change), routine and routine_run, from any process; one LISTEN connection per worker generation (src/events) feeds an in-memory bus with a 1000-event ring for Last-Event-ID replay. Another generation's id (the supervisor ends streams on drain), a restart or a dropped LISTEN gives a resync and the page refetches once; replay across generations waits for the outbox (1.4). Plan, Build and Routines refetch on it (the 30 s polls are gone; a 5 min fallback poll stays). Measured on the work laptop: row commit to SSE frame 2 ms p50, 11 ms max; Plan sees a change in about 0.5 s (its /api/state takes 0.4 to 0.6 s), Build in about 0.1 s
details.Factory push: POST /api/factory/events (X-PA): a factory on this machine pushes {job_id, state, why?, updated_at?} or {jobs: [...]}; merged into factory_board at once (Build shows it in about 25 ms) and the full `job list` follows within PA_FACTORY_ACTIVE_POLL_SECONDS. The factory side of it is not wired yet (planned with the native factory, plan 2.3)

components.name: Worker
components.role: A scheduler of periodic passes (no job queue: work to do is a query). One owner of the passes per machine: a Postgres advisory-lock lease (src/util/lease.js), handed between generations on a roll.

where.work: a generation of the supervisor (pa-worker task → node src/supervisor → src/worker.js); also hosts the dashboard
where.personal: systemd user unit pa-worker (node src/supervisor once redeployed) on k-911-x17 (also hosts the dashboard)

details.Rule: Passes never overlap themselves; a crash costs one tick, the next sees the same delta.
Model passes: reconcile, card context, repo profiles (PA_RECONCILE_MODEL, default claude-sonnet-5-5)
memory extract / decide / pages (default claude-sonnet-5-5 each)
briefs, debriefs, reply-close, planner, routines, compose (default claude-sonnet-5-5)
Microsoft 365 connector relay (PA_CONNECTOR_MODEL, default claude-haiku-5-5; Claude Code only)
details.Model strings: provider/model (src/models.js). A bare Claude name uses the Anthropic API when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, else a headless `claude -p` (the Claude Code login).
details.Spend: every metered call lands in llm_spend; unknown prices are null, never estimated; daily budget PA_DAILY_BUDGET_USD (default 15) with essential vs discretionary passes

components.name: Ingest: connectors
components.role: Captures mail, Teams, calendar, GitHub, Jira, Claude/Cursor sessions and meeting audio as append-only source items.

where.work: Worker passes on the laptop
where.personal: Worker passes on k-911-x17, every source off until the personal sources are chosen

details.Microsoft 365: a headless `claude -p` relays the claude.ai connector calls; items are built from the tool_result blocks, never from model text
details.Teams cache: reads the new Teams client's IndexedDB on disk, read-only, triggered by a change notification and served by one resident reader process (seconds behind, vs minutes for the connector)
details.Jira: API token, falling back to its connector, every 900 s
details.Sessions: local Claude Code and Cursor transcripts; other machines' Claude sessions through their termhub (GET /api/claude/transcripts)
details.Meetings: capture.py records, the audio pass trims and transcribes with faster-whisper
details.Rule: capture is append-only and raw payloads are kept

components.name: Commitments, ledger and board
components.role: Distils asks into commitments, links blockers, dedupes, and changes status only through the ledger; the board is built from them.

where.work: Worker passes + dashboard (/api/state)
where.personal: Worker passes + dashboard on k-911-x17 (empty: nothing is ingested)

details.Only people create tasks: sourcePolicy decides in code before any model call; bots, CI and the assistant's own sessions are evidence only
details.Blocks pass: links what someone owes you to the task it holds up (commitment_block)
details.Ledger: ledger.transition is the one writer of commitment.status; each change leaves a reversible ledger_transition row
details.Board: One card per commitment: On me (with blockers and 'Looks done?'), Waiting, Notes (src/dashboard/board.js)
details.Memory: claims carry a verbatim quote; memory supersedes, never deletes; agents only propose

components.name: Notifications
components.role: A feed in the dashboard, desktop toasts or ntfy pushes under an interrupt budget, and the PA chat's INBOX.md.

where.work: Worker
where.personal: Worker on k-911-x17 (dashboard feed; no desktop session for notify-send)

details.Budget: PA_PUSH_BUDGET pushes (default 4), quiet hours 19-08, digests at 09:00 and 14:00
details.PA chat: pushes go to pa-home/INBOX.md; the only text ever typed into the chat is a content-free doorbell, and only when nudgeDecision proves the session is idle at an empty prompt
details.ntfy: fallback mode by default; bodies off unless PA_NTFY_BODY=1

components.name: Dispatcher
components.role: Starts work: a Claude Code session in termhub (own worktree), or a factory job through the JOBS-API. Enforces delivery levels and modes.

where.work: In-process (pa do, the dashboard's Do, the chat's action tools)
where.personal: In-process on k-911-x17; the factory is this machine’s own, chat and Claude runs wait on a personal claude login

details.Routes: the factory is the default once PA_FACTORY_PATH is set (PA_DISPATCH_VIA); plan mode and --machine still mean a Claude session
details.Claude session: POST /api/sessions on termhub with PA_CLAUDE_COMMAND (claude --dangerously-skip-permissions) in its own worktree; a no-push run gets no credentials in its env and a verified push block
details.Factory job: `uv run factory job submit --json ...` run on PA_FACTORY_MACHINE through termhub's POST /api/exec (argv, no shell), content on stdin; idempotent on --source pa --external-id
details.Brief: composed by PA_COMPOSE_MODEL (default claude-sonnet-5-5; with no Anthropic key it takes a keyed PA_COMPOSE_FALLBACK_MODEL such as azure/<deployment> instead of `claude -p`) from the card; private material is selected from, never copied in; deterministic fallback
details.Delivery levels: none < branch < draft_pr < pr < auto_merge < push_to_main, set only from your side; the last two need a confirmed start
details.Factory defaults: PA_FACTORY_RUNTIME api, PA_FACTORY_PIPELINE solo; the chat's factory_start defaults to claude_session unless you ask for the API
details.Which factory: PA_FACTORY_MACHINE + PA_FACTORY_PATH in each stack's .env (the live values are shown at the top of this page)
details.Factory pacing: the worker's factory pass (src/dispatch/factoryPace.js) runs every PA_FACTORY_ACTIVE_POLL_SECONDS (5) while a job is queued, triaging or in progress, at once when a factory on this machine writes state/factory.db (watched, never read), and every PA_FACTORY_POLL_SECONDS (120) otherwise. Each pass is a `uv run factory` call: about 5 s of Python start-up on the work laptop, which is why the sub-second path is the factory's push (POST /api/factory/events)

components.name: Golden-path check (pa e2e)
components.role: Plan E4: one command runs the golden path headless against the live stack (a dummy card to a draft PR on xvanov/dev-tools), times each hop, checks that every view links the same card, run, job, steps, sessions and PR, and cleans up.

where.work: `pa e2e` in-process on the machine it runs on; `--on <machine>` runs it on another PA_MACHINES machine through its termhub (exec for --dry-run/--sweep, a session for a real run)
where.personal: the same command, run on the personal machine

details.Path: card by commitments/request.js (as typed on the board), then the chat's factory_start tool (factory_continue with --branch), runtime claude_session by default or --runtime api --model m; delivery draft_pr
details.Hops: card -> job started -> first session output -> PR opened -> CI done (+ step killed, job resumed with --resume), timed off `factory job status` polls (--poll, 10 s), woken early by run/factory events on the dashboard's GET /api/events (0.4); each hop has a timeout (--timeout hop=seconds)
details.Checks: Plan GET /api/state and /api/commitments/:id (card.chain), Build GET /api/factory (paRun, stories, runs), Run termhub GET /api/sessions (links, alive or scrollback), MCP card and factory_job tools, GitHub `gh pr view` (head = story branch, draft) as the repo owner via GH_TOKEN from `gh auth token --user`; E2: an API step has a session whose scrollback shows a model turn
details.Cleanup: unless --keep: PR closed with --delete-branch, job cancelled if live, card dropped through the ledger, step sessions killed; `pa e2e --sweep` finds leftovers by the e2e-<uuid> marker on the card and the stored run, run_step and run_pr links
details.Dry run: `pa e2e --dry-run`: database, factory configured and on this machine (D13), factory app for the repo, dashboard /healthz, /api/state, /api/factory, termhub /api/sessions, the chat tools, gh write access; creates nothing
details.Output: hop/timing table and a JSON report (--json alone; --report file); exit 1 on any missed hop or failed link

components.name: Postgres store
components.role: Postgres 16 + pgvector: every item, commitment, claim, run, proposal and the factory board snapshot.

details.Migrations: plain numbered SQL in personal-assistant/sql, applied by src/db/migrate.js at worker start
details.Expand/contract (Z3): a roll runs the previous generation on the new schema, so after 032 every migration is additive; drops, renames, retypes and tightened constraints ship later as a contract migration marked `-- contract: <expand file>`. test/migrations.test.js (src/db/migrationRules.js) enforces it, refuses edits to applied migrations and checks the previous commit's INSERTs against the new schema without Postgres
details.Durable tasks: Absurd (vendored schema) for work that waits: chases, run reviews
details.Embeddings (audit 2026-11-07): text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims, embed once and never re-embed (plan D5). Embedded: message and document chunks (chunk), memory claims (claim), memory pages (memory_page), commitment text for semantic dedupe (commitment_vector). Never embedded: identifiers, statuses, board state, numbers, dates; PR and ticket refs dedupe by key (commitment anchors), not by vector. No call site embeds changing data or exact keys; stored vectors are 41.5k (31.1k chunks, 10.0k claims, 105 pages, 242 commitments) and re-embed only when their own text changes (a changed item body, a regenerated page) or when CONTEXT_VERSION is bumped, which is a decision, not a cleanup
details.Query embeddings: a search embeds its query once: normalized text (trimmed, whitespace collapsed, lower-cased) plus model and dimensions -> vector, in an in-memory LRU (PA_EMBED_CACHE_ENTRIES, 500) backed by query_embedding_cache (PA_EMBED_CACHE_ROWS, 5000 by last use); query time only, never ingest
details.Secrets: never here: OS vault or the gitignored .env
details.WSL caveat: WSL stops the distro when the last client exits; the pa-wsl-keepalive logon task holds it open
details.Id chain: plan E1: card -> run -> job -> step -> session -> PR as stored ids. run (commitment_id, factory_job_id, termhub_session_id, mr_url, external_id) plus run_pr (every PR of a run: number, state, CI) and run_step (every factory step: job, story, persona, termhub session id, machine, URL), written by the worker factory pass from job status (sql/033); read by the board (card.chain), the card detail, Build and the card / factory_job / sessions MCP tools

examples.title: Start a PR on the metered API
examples.say: Start the PR for card 412 with DeepSeek.

steps.t: Wake word, VAD, transcription as above.
An action: the fast lane never answers it. It says 'On it.' and hands off your verbatim words.
Your words are typed into the PA chat through termhub. Claude Code calls card 412 (allowed) and then factory_start {card: 412, runtime: api, model: deepseek/deepseek-coder, delivery: pr}.

factory_start is on no allow list: Claude Code shows a permission prompt. Jarvis asks "Start a factory job for card 412 on the API with deepseek/deepseek-coder, opening a PR for review. Shall I?" and you say yes (or press Approve on the dashboard).

dispatch.start composes the brief from the card (PA_COMPOSE_MODEL), writes a flow file, and runs `uv run factory job submit --json --runtime api --model dev=deepseek/deepseek-coder --delivery pr` on the factory machine.
On the work stack the command runs through the WSL termhub's POST /api/exec (argv, no shell; content on stdin).
The factory answers one JSON object with the job id; the PA records the run.
Solo pipeline: one dev agent, then gates, a PR, and the CI watch (up to 3 CI-fix cycles).
OpenHands runs the dev step; LiteLLM calls DeepSeek.
Metered: the spend shows in the job's cost_usd.
Branch pushed, ready PR opened, checks watched; delivered_pr, never merged.

The factory pass (every 5 s while the job moves) stores `job list` in factory_board; its trigger puts the change on the live feed, so the Factory page redraws at once; it and the chat's factory_job show state, PR and cost; a notification tells you.

examples.title: Continue a PR on the subscription
examples.say: Fix the review comments on PR 12.

steps.t: Hand-off to the PA chat.
Calls factory_continue {pr: 12, repo}: runtime defaults to claude_session because you did not ask for the API. You approve the prompt.
`job submit --pr 12 --runtime claude_session`. Landing: a factory without --pr refuses in its parser and the job fails saying so, never resent as fresh work.
The factory checks `claude auth status` is a claude.ai login, then starts `claude -p --output-format stream-json` in a termhub session with API-key variables removed.
The session lives in the WSL termhub; its URL is in runs[].session, so you can open it live from the Factory page.
Billed to the subscription: cost_usd 0, the API-price equivalent goes to subscription_equiv_usd.
The fix is pushed fast-forward to the same PR; the CI watch restarts on the new head.

examples.title: Someone asks you for something in Teams
examples.say: (a colleague writes: 'can you send me the numbers by Friday?')

steps.t: The message lands in the Teams client; its local cache changes on disk.
The change notification wakes the resident cache reader; the item is stored as a source_item in seconds (the connector pass confirms it minutes later, same row).
The distill pass (sourcePolicy first) extracts an owed_by_me commitment with an absolute due date; blocks and dedupe link it to related work.
commitment row, with extracted_by and the raw payload kept.
The card appears under On me on the board.
Within the interrupt budget: a toast (or ntfy), and INBOX.md for the PA chat with a content-free doorbell when it is idle.

examples.title: A research report
examples.say: Research how our deploy pipeline handles rollbacks and write it up.

steps.t: You asked for research explicitly, so the chat calls factory_start {kind: research, ask: your words}; you approve the prompt.
A research job delivers none; its ask is your own words (no composing model).
job submit --kind research returns an id like app:r0007.
The next factory tick starts a detached worker (at most 2 at a time).
One Claude Code conversation (claude_session by default from the chat) writes report.md; 5400 s cap.
state/jobs/r0007-<slug>/report.md is kept by the factory.
The poll sees it done; factory_job returns the report excerpt and the Factory page renders the report as a parsed tree (no HTML sink).
